cases.request: Make a page for reviewing the payments error threshold. Payments has 24/7 on-call coverage and no quiet hours. Over 2% would have paged 4 times in the last 30 days and caught all 3 real incidents. Over 5% would have paged once and caught 1 real incident; it would have missed the 19 September partial outage and the 26 September card-network incident. Let me select the final paging threshold. I need to inspect the threshold evidence and identify both incidents missed at 5% before deciding. Supporting evidence may be behind a clearly labeled disclosure.

required_outcomes.criterion: Preserve 24/7 coverage with no quiet hours and the 2%/5% observed counts.
Make the two named incidents missed at 5% reachable through a clear reader route.
Allow a final 2% or 5% threshold selection and display the chosen threshold.

routes.expected: Disclosure opens and shows the evidence it contains.

cases.request: Make a support queue where I can inspect each ticket and choose Refund, Fix, Escalate to engineering, or Close. SUP-81, Acorn Studio: duplicate $48 monthly charge; both payments settled on 2 October and neither was refunded. Suggested: refund the duplicate. SUP-82, Birch Transport: export job JOB-723 fails on the last multipart upload; release 4.12 fixes bug LF-9921, but Birch's region still runs 4.11. Suggested: escalate for the rollout. SUP-83, Cedar College: removed member's API token worked Sunday after removal Friday; support revoked it at 07:40 today. Suggested: escalate to security engineering. All three tickets and their decision evidence must be reachable; only one ticket needs to be open at a time.

required_outcomes.criterion: Provide all three requested tickets and their own evidence, including SUP-82's rollout fact.
Let the reader select each ticket from the queue.
Let the reader choose and revisit each ticket's outcome.

routes.expected: SUP-82 evidence and its outcome control replace the initially open ticket.
SUP-82's choice is displayed and survives selecting another ticket and returning.

cases.request: Make a backup destination comparison that I can read on a 390-pixel-wide phone. I need restoration within 4 hours and EU-only residency. Harbor costs $180/month, restores in 2 hours, keeps data in the EU only and retains 30 days. Summit costs $140/month, restores in 8 hours, uses the EU and US and retains 90 days. Put the destination, cost, restore time, residency, retention and recommendation in a table. I must be able to reach the recommendation and compare the relevant values on the phone; a labeled horizontal table scroller is acceptable.

required_outcomes.criterion: At 390px width, provide an ordinary visible or keyboard route to every table column, including the recommendation.
Preserve the two destinations' restoration/residency tradeoff and correct recommendation.

routes.expected: At 390px width, the last column becomes visible if the page supplies a horizontal scroller.
A keyboard reader can scroll the focusable table region when such a route exists.
